title: Mifepristone REMS prescriber certification, guidelines for use and the Patient Agreement Form
rule_summary: The approved Mifepristone REMS Program document (most recent modification 09/2025) requires that healthcare providers who prescribe mifepristone be specially certified. To become certified a healthcare provider must review the Prescribing Information and complete a Prescriber Agreement Form, by signing which the prescriber agrees to having the ability to assess the duration of pregnancy accurately, the ability to diagnose ectopic pregnancies, and the ability to provide surgical intervention in cases of incomplete abortion or severe bleeding, or to have made plans to provide such care through others, together with the ability to assure patient access to medical facilities equipped to provide blood transfusions and resuscitation, if necessary, and agrees to follow the guidelines for use. As a condition of certification the prescriber must ensure that the Patient Agreement Form is reviewed with the patient and the risks of the treatment regimen are fully explained, that any questions the patient may have before receiving mifepristone are answered, that the healthcare provider and the patient sign the Patient Agreement Form, that the patient is provided with a copy of the Patient Agreement Form and the Medication Guide, that the signed Patient Agreement Form is placed in the patient's medical record, and that any deaths are reported to the Mifepristone Sponsor that provided the mifepristone, identifying the patient by a non-identifiable reference and including the NDC and lot number. If mifepristone will be dispensed by a certified pharmacy the prescriber must provide the certified pharmacy a signed Prescriber Agreement Form, assess the appropriateness of dispensing when contacted by a certified pharmacy about a patient who will receive mifepristone more than 4 calendar days after the prescription was received by the certified pharmacy, and obtain the NDC and lot number of the package the patient received if the prescriber becomes aware of the patient's death. A certified prescriber who dispenses mifepristone or supervises its dispensing must provide an authorized distributor with a signed Prescriber Agreement Form, ensure that the NDC and lot number from each package dispensed are recorded in the patient's record, and ensure that healthcare providers under the prescriber's supervision follow the guidelines. Mifepristone must be dispensed to patients with evidence or other documentation of safe use conditions as ensured by the certified prescriber in signing the Prescriber Agreement Form, and the patient must sign a Patient Agreement Form indicating that the patient has received, read and been provided a copy of it and has received counseling from the healthcare provider regarding the risk of serious complications. In the REMS the terms sign and signature include electronic signatures. FDA states that the program does not require patients to see a health care provider in person before obtaining mifepristone, and that some states allow health care providers other than physicians to prescribe medications and health care providers should check their individual state laws.
exam_relevance: Tests which duties the REMS gives the certified prescriber rather than the pharmacy: the qualifications attested in the Prescriber Agreement Form, the Patient Agreement Form, and providing the patient a copy of it and of the Medication Guide.

exceptions: The duties toward a certified pharmacy apply when mifepristone will be dispensed by a certified pharmacy, and the additional duties of a dispensing or supervising prescriber apply when the certified prescriber dispenses mifepristone or supervises its dispensing.
common_confusions: Assuming the program requires an in-person visit before a patient obtains mifepristone; FDA states that it does not.

Placing the Patient Agreement Form duties on the pharmacy; the REMS makes the certified prescriber ensure the form is reviewed, signed, copied to the patient and placed in the patient's medical record.
Treating certification as a physician-only status; the REMS certifies healthcare providers who prescribe, and FDA notes that some states allow providers other than physicians to prescribe.
